title: Seat a Mini-ITX server board on four locating standoffs
instruction: Seat the Mini-ITX motherboard on all four standoffs with its rear ports in the opening, then release it.
context: Robots that build and service data-center hardware would speed up AI compute build-out. Mini-ITX server boards such as Supermicro's X11SDV-4C-TLN2F (Xeon D, 170 x 170 mm) are the motherboards of compact edge servers like the SuperServer E300-9D; integrators and field technicians seat a new or replacement board in the chassis on its four standoffs, with its rear I/O through the chassis opening, before screwing it down. The board is held only by its edges: it is lowered flat so all four locating pins enter their 3.96 mm holes together, then let go. A board set down off the pins rests on them and is not seated; one pushed in at an angle catches a pin.
setup: Unpowered computer assembly station; tabletop z=0.7475 m. A 210 x 210 x 4 mm black ESD rubber mat is centred at (0.100,0,0.7495) m. A 240 x 240 x 12 mm fixed aluminium assembly plate is centred at (0.350,0,0.7535) m. Four brass standoff bases of radius 7 mm and height 24 mm carry coaxial 2.4 mm diameter, 6 mm high cylindrical locating pins. Pin and standoff centres follow the Mini-ITX C/F/H/J pattern at board-local x,y positions in mm: C=(74.84,-78.65), F=(51.98,78.83), H=(-80.10,-78.65), J=(-80.10,78.83), relative to target board origin (0.350,0) m; standoff centres are at z=0.7715 m and pin centres at z=0.7865 m. A fixed open-topped steel rear I/O channel is centred at x=0.455 m and is 100 mm wide between its sides. The board is a Mini-ITX server board: a Supermicro X11SDV-4C-TLN2F (or an unpowered retired unit of it), handled with an ESD wrist strap and nitrile gloves, the robot's grippers padded with ESD-safe foam. In the simulation it is a 170 x 170 x 1.6 mm green FR-4 Mini-ITX board, mass 0.44 kg, has four 3.96 mm diameter circular through-holes at those positions, a plastic CPU cover and slots, and a 38 x 60 x 18 mm rear I/O housing. It starts flat on the mat with body origin (0.100,0,0.7523) m and zero yaw. Its seated body origin is (0.350,0,0.7843) m. Two 16 x 26 x 18 mm black polymer protective edge clamps are attached at board-local (-0.060,+0.079,+0.010) and (+0.050,-0.079,+0.010) m, clear of the holes, and provide gripping surfaces. All parts start stationary.
scoring: Measured at the end, with checks a person can make on the real fixture. 0 if the board centre is more than 20 mm from its seated position, tilted over 8 degrees or yawed over 12 degrees (a photo from above with a scale). 0.25 inside that zone. 0.5: every locating pin has entered its hole, seen from above as the pin's tip inside the hole outline (in the simulation, each pin axis within 0.98 mm of its hole centre at both PCB faces: the 0.78 mm radial clearance plus 0.2 mm for the strips that approximate the round hole), and every hole within 6 mm of its standoff top. 0.75: all four pins engaged and the board seated: a 1.0 mm feeler gauge does not enter between the board and the top of any standoff, tilt and yaw at most 3 degrees, and the rear I/O housing through the opening (its tip at least as far as the wall's inner face, x 0.453 m, and centred within 30 mm). Because the pins and the board collide, a board seated on all four standoffs has all four pins through its holes. 1.0: that pose still for 1 second and both grippers open with their tool points at least 60 mm from the board. Screws and power-on are outside the trial.
reset_notes: Put the motherboard back flat on the ESD mat at the stated starting pose. Inspect that every hole and locating pin is unobstructed. The fixed bench and rear wall do not move.
fidelity: The board is full-size with the standard Mini-ITX C/F/H/J hole locations and 3.96 mm circular mounting holes. The simulator approximates each round aperture with narrow collision strips and represents the PCB, ports, and attached protective clamps as one rigid body. The fixture uses 2.4 mm round locating pins with 0.78 mm nominal radial clearance; pin detents, screw fastening, and electrical contact are not modelled.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (seed 0, ended at the 2,500-step limit); scripted demo: 1.0 at step 299 of 2,500. Both on this task.py (SHA-256 prefix 24da1ad9817a) under the revised scorer.
